title: BMS / DJMax Keysound Slicer UX Audit
report_markdown:
# BMS / DJMax Keysound Slicer UX audit (research snapshot: 2026-09-18)

## 1. Comparison table

| Tool | Workflow (observed) | Top 3 pain points / limits | Max slices / snap | Export method |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sayaslicer | Open/drag audio; add or import markers; optionally set offset, snap, zero-crossing, tail removal/fade; preview; copy BMSE/iBMSC data or keysound list; export keysounds; save project. [GitHub README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer) | (1) Zero-crossing moves markers and can break arbitrary-resolution iBMSC paste; (2) BMSE compatibility rounds to nearest 192nd; (3) very-large-file loading was a historical failure, fixed by backend overhaul. [README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer) · [issue #5](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/issues/5) · [release](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/releases) | No slice-count ceiling stated; snapping 1/1–1/192. [README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer) | Individual keysound export (`M`), clipboard/BMS list export, BMSE/iBMSC clipboard. [README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer) |
| Woslicer II | Load WAV; set BPM/offset/grid; place markers; preview; batch-export; export clipboard and paste into BMSE, with starting definition controlled by A/S. [guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html) | Repetitive file/definition ceremony; rough slicing can create pop artifacts; guides warn about long keysounds and require manual tail decisions. [guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3) · [Qiita](https://qiita.com/yuinore/items/79db943d2e3447adee71) | Documented shortcuts include grid Q/W, but a numeric maximum was not verified in the II guide; III guide documents 192. [guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html) · [guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3) | Batch WAV export and clipboard export to BMSE. [guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html) |
| Woslicer III | Drag/drop WAV; set BPM, offset and grid; click bar lines to cut; preview; write WAV and `.wos`; reload `.wos` for reuse; define WAVs in BMSE and paste sequence data. [guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3) | Definition numbering/order depends on Explorer and BMSE selection order; reusing definitions is explicitly time-consuming; rough slicing has pop/reverse-tail tradeoffs. [guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/) · [Qiita](https://qiita.com/yuinore/items/79db943d2e3447adee71) | Grid maximum 192 subdivisions/measure; filenames can exceed 3 digits, but no total slice ceiling is stated. [guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3) | WAV files, `.wos` project/settings, clipboard sequence data. [guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3) |
| BMHelper / Mid2BMS | Import MIDI/notes; rearrange notes before rendering; use external audio render and Woslicer; copy cut positions; then automate/assist BMS placement. BMHelper itself does not slice audio. [BMHelper](https://excln.github.io/bmhelper.html) · [Mid2BMS wiki](https://wiki.mid2bms.net/%E4%BB%96%E3%83%83%E3%83%BC%E3%83%AB/Be-Music%20Helper) | MIDI incompatibilities; tool choice/documentation friction; still depends on external slicer and BMS definitions. [BMHelper](https://excln.github.io/bmhelper.html) · [wiki](https://wiki.mid2bms.net/%E4%BB%96%E3%83%83%E3%83%BC%E3%83%AB/Be-Music%20Helper) | No verified global slice/snap ceiling in fetched docs; BMS compatibility is constrained by editor resolution. [BMS checklist](https://wcko87.github.io/bms-checklist/) | Clipboard positions/sequence and generated WAV/definitions through the surrounding workflow. [BMHelper guide](https://w.atwiki.jp/coolnaurl/pages/19.html) |
| PTSEQUENCER / DJMAX-era workflow | Treat keysounds as numbered platform assets, then arrange notes/keysound references in the target chart format. | PTSEQUENCER-era DJMAX is documented at 1023 keysounds; older same-track playback can cut off the previous sample; adapting richer audio becomes an optimization exercise. [NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C) | 1023 keysounds for the cited DJMAX/PTSEQUENCER-era tooling; not a slicer snap limit. [NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C) | Platform-specific numbered keysound assets; exact PTSEQUENCER export procedure was not published in the fetched sources. |
| sound-slicer | Prepare source WAV plus text/MIDI; slice into a `wav` subfolder; generate BMS clipboard data; paste/transpose it. Rhythmic mode produces one slice per MIDI event; melodic mode can reuse a small set of slices. [README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer) | Rhythmic mode can generate one slice per note (1000 notes → 1000 slices example); both modes do not support BPM changes; requires external scripts/SoX-style project layout. [README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer) | No numeric snap limit; no BPM-change support. [README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer) | Individual WAV slices plus generated BMS clipboard file. [README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer) |

## 2. Problem inventory

### Timeline / alignment

- **P0 — one view does not reconcile audio time with chart time.** Existing workflows make users set BPM/offset/grid in a slicer and then paste into BMSE; Woslicer’s guide defines offset as choosing the source start and says leading silence must be consistent across parts. A dual waveform + chart ruler with one playhead would remove this cross-app alignment step. [Woslicer guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3)
- **P1 — coarse/fine-grid mismatch is silent and dangerous.** iBMSC export can preserve over-192nd markers, while BMSE export rounds to the nearest 192nd; ubmsc’s default max partition of 192 can snap finer objects on save and produce overlap warnings. [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer) · [BMS checklist](https://wcko87.github.io/bms-checklist/)
- **P1 — playback placement is inherently approximate.** Sayaslicer’s playback-marker PR says Q/W placement may be imprecise and must be fine-tuned; it added a moving line because users had difficulty knowing where they were in the waveform. [PR #11](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/pull/11)
- **P1 — tail handling is musically consequential.** The Woslicer workflow explicitly makes the next bar the last cut to preserve a snare tail, then deletes the resulting silent key; a Qiita investigation describes reverse-extension/zero material intended to manage abrupt cuts but capable of producing pops. [Woslicer guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3) · [Qiita](https://qiita.com/yuinore/items/79db943d2e3447adee71)

### Interface / workflow

- **P0 — export ceremony and file bookkeeping.** The documented path is render/cut WAVs → put them in the BMS folder → define WAVs in BMSE → paste sequence → manually verify naming/order. Dragging multiple files depends on both Explorer order and the preselected BMSE definition start. [Woslicer guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/) · [BMHelper guide](https://w.atwiki.jp/coolnaurl/pages/19.html)
- **P1 — reuse is not first-class.** Woslicer’s `.wos` helps reload numeric settings and positions, but the guide still describes entering a definition number, pasting into BMSE, and recycling identical definitions as time-consuming. [Woslicer guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3)
- **P1 — repetitive editor operations require external clipboard helpers.** BMS Clipboarder exists specifically for programs operating on editor clipboard data and includes note-moving/BGM operations. [BMS Clipboarder](https://github.com/bemusic/bms-clipboarder)
- **P2 — install/platform friction.** Sayaslicer is cross-platform, but its macOS build is unsigned and requires quarantine/security workarounds. [README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer)

### Settings / feedback

- **P0 — zero-cross is a tradeoff, not a free quality switch.** It can reduce clicks but moves markers and therefore changes chart timing/clipboard behavior. The product should preview the timing delta and allow per-slice override. [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer)
- **P1 — automatic detection needs correction affordances.** Fruity Slicer documents zero-cross checking specifically for click/pop artifacts and warns that misplaced or missing markers require manual fine-tuning. [Image-Line Fruity Slicer manual](https://www.image-line.com/fl-studio-learning/fl-studio-online-manual/html/plugins/Fruity%20Slicer.htm)
- **P1 — resolution controls are tool-specific and confusing.** Woslicer III documents a 192 maximum; Sayaslicer exposes 1/1–1/192 and has separate BMSE/iBMSC compatibility semantics. [Woslicer guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3) · [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer)
- **P2 — BPM changes remain a gap.** sound-slicer explicitly does not support BPM changes, while Sayaslicer calls better BPM-change support a planned feature. [sound-slicer README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer) · [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer)

### Backend / format

- **P0 — destructive export multiplies assets and creates consistency risk.** sound-slicer’s documented layout is one source plus a `wav` directory containing many numbered WAVs; Woslicer/BMSE workflows similarly generate and then define those files. A virtual `{sourceFile,startMs,endMs}` slice avoids intermediate files until finalization. [sound-slicer README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer) · [Woslicer guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3)
- **P0 — key-count ceilings force audible compromises.** NamuWiki reports 1023 keysounds in the cited DJMAX/PTSEQUENCER-era tooling, 1295 base-36 BMS slots, and BMSE’s pilot base-62 expansion to 3843; it also explains that same-track playback can cut off an earlier sample. [NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C)
- **P1 — BMS still has playback semantics unlike a virtual-note model.** NamuWiki says a same-number BMS sample restarts from the beginning and that over-definition may be used to avoid this, consuming valuable keysound slots. [NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C)
- **P1 — long files and formats can break tools.** Sayaslicer issue #5 documents >2GB files becoming unusable due to signed integer overflow; the later backend overhaul fixed very-large-file loading and added formats such as Opus. [issue #5](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/issues/5) · [release notes](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/releases)
- **P1 — distribution limits feed back into slicing.** A BMS production checklist says keysounds over 60s are blocked from LR2IR, recommends ~40-second splits, and recommends OGG to reduce large WAV packages. [BMS checklist](https://wcko87.github.io/bms-checklist/)

## 3. What Sayaslicer did right vs Woslicer (keep these)

**Keep from Sayaslicer:** cross-platform delivery; drag/drop; project save/load; arbitrary 1/1–1/192 snapping; separate BMSE and iBMSC clipboard paths; zero-crossing, fade/tail processing; marker copy/paste; undo/redo; keysound-list export; marker navigation; waveform zoom/y-scale; and a playback line. These are all documented features or release/PR changes, not inferred marketing claims. [README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer) · [release](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/releases) · [PR #10](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/pull/10) · [PR #11](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/pull/11)

**Keep from Woslicer:** the extremely direct bar-line interaction (left click add/right click remove), keyboard-first preview/export, `.wos` as a portable recipe of settings + markers, and clipboard output that eliminates one-note-at-a-time placement. [Woslicer II guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html) · [Woslicer III guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3)

**Improve rather than copy:** make “definition reuse” a stable object identity in a slice library; do not require Explorer ordering or manually typed starting definition numbers; make zero-cross/tail changes visible as timing/audio previews; and preserve source audio non-destructively.

## 4. Top 10 recommendations for DJMax Studio Slicer

1. **P0 — Make virtual slices the canonical model.** Store `{sourceFile,startMs,endMs}` plus processing overrides; export WAV/OGG only on finalize. This directly removes the documented WAV-folder/definition bookkeeping. [sound-slicer README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer) · [Woslicer guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)
2. **P0 — Ship the proposed dual timeline.** Put waveform and chart preview on synchronized rulers with a shared playhead, BPM/offset markers, and ms + beat labels. Existing users must translate between Woslicer and BMSE and playback placement can be imprecise. [Woslicer guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3) · [Sayaslicer PR #11](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/pull/11)
3. **P0 — Make snap explicit and lossless.** Offer 1/4 through 1/192 (and an “off/free” mode), show the quantization delta, and warn before a target format rounds finer markers. The 192-vs-arbitrary iBMSC/BMSE split is a proven failure mode. [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer) · [BMS checklist](https://wcko87.github.io/bms-checklist/)
4. **P0 — Add a Slice Library with stable IDs and reuse.** One source segment can be referenced by many notes without over-definition or duplicate exports; include search, audition, occurrence count, and “replace all.” This targets Woslicer’s time-consuming definition recycling and BMS slot pressure. [Woslicer guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3) · [NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C)
5. **P1 — Provide per-slice Zero-X, fade, tail and normalize overrides.** Zero-crossing can move timing; Fruity Slicer’s manual confirms automatic marker correction still needs manual refinement. Show original vs adjusted boundary. [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer) · [Fruity Slicer manual](https://www.image-line.com/fl-studio-learning/fl-studio-online-manual.htm)
6. **P1 — Use safe guided auto-advance.** Grid/Beat/Off modes, with a keyboard shortcut and an audible/visual confirmation after each cut. This preserves Woslicer’s keyboard speed while reducing accidental silent double-placement. [Woslicer II guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html)
7. **P1 — Make tail policy first-class.** Offer “next onset,” fixed ms, zero-cross, fade, and preserve-tail modes; flag overlaps and possible pop/cutoff. The source workflow currently relies on manual “last cut” decisions and cleanup of silent files. [Woslicer guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3) · [Qiita](https://qiita.com/yuinore/items/79db943d2e3447adee71)
8. **P1 — Implement BPM maps, not one BPM.** Support imported MIDI tempo maps and partial BPM changes, with beat/bar grid recalculation. BPM-change absence is explicit in sound-slicer and better support remains planned in Sayaslicer. [sound-slicer README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer) · [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer)
9. **P1 — Add round-trip “Import to Studio / Export back” adapters.** Keep source IDs and boundaries through BMS clipboard, RESPECT and TECHNIKA modes; validate key-count/format constraints before export. Existing clipboard approaches are one-way and require editor/file ordering. [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer) · [BMSE/Woslicer guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)
10. **P2 — Make capacity and finalization visible.** Show projected slice count, per-mode key-slot usage, file size, long-slice warnings, OGG/WAV choice, and a preflight report. BMS/LR2 and DJMAX-era limits demonstrably change how creators must cut and package audio. [BMS checklist](https://wcko87.github.io/bms-checklist/) · [NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C)

### Mode-switch recommendation

Implement BMS / RESPECT / TECHNIKA as explicit export/playback modes, not merely skins. The fetched evidence shows materially different constraints: BMS historically uses base-36 and newer base-62 identifiers; DJMAX-era tooling has a cited 1023-key limit; older DJMAX-style same-track playback can interrupt a prior sample, while the NamuWiki account says Technika 2 changed to non-interfering inputs. [NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C)

## Evidence limits

I found no populated Sayaslicer issue list in the fetched GitHub Issues view (it displayed “No results”), so a “top 10 issues” ranking would be fabricated; the report instead uses the repository README, release notes and the specific issue/PR pages that were available. I also did not find a fetched PTSEQUENCER manual with a step-by-step export procedure, nor a reliable accessible YouTube-comment corpus; those fields are explicitly marked as not verified rather than inferred.
